text:
Ava (People Ops): FYI — helping coordinate a short sabbatical for Maya. She plans to be in Bali for ~10 weeks, doing ~10 hrs/week of paid consulting for a US-based client while still on Redwood payroll. She asked whether the WFH stipend continues and whether this creates any tax/employer obligations. Any quick flags?
Maya Patel: correct — 10 weeks (late May -> early Aug), still Redwood employee, not changing home base. Client work is a freelance retainer, paid to her personally via Stripe. WFH stipend would help cover coworking + local internet while traveling.
Marco (Payroll): couple of immediate Qs: 1) exact dates, 2) will payroll still be processed to the same bank account/currency, 3) is her home base declared as CA/US? Also, outside-income to her personally could create withholding/reporting requirements depending on country and whether she becomes tax resident.
Maya Patel: dates 2026-05-22 -> 2026-08-01. Payroll to same US bank. Home base remains OR (Oregon).
Priya (Legal): high-level: Indonesia has a 183-day rule for tax residency, but there are other triggers (work performed in-country, economic employer nexus). Short stays under ~90 days often avoid residency but don't guarantee no local obligations — e.g., some vendors/contractors/local regs can require registration or withholding sooner. Also watch for local business-license/visa rules when doing client work locally. Not formal advice — we'll need local counsel if payroll flags emerge.
Jon (Benefits): on the stipend side: our current WFH stipend policy says stipend continues for remote work that doesn't change home base; however, we have a cap for extended travel where we ask for notification > 30 days. For sabbatical vs PTO differences, we treat paid sabbatical or unpaid leave differently. Since she's still actively working (part-time) for a client and remains employed, I'd treat this as temporary remote work — stipend should remain but needs manager sign-off.
Devon (Manager): I approve the sabbatical time off pattern and stipend continuation pending payroll/legal check. We want Maya to maintain contact cadence.
Marco (Payroll): action items from payroll side: 1) run quick country risk check (Indonesia) for employer reporting/filing, 2) confirm no change to pay method prevents extra banking compliance, 3) flag for potential need to treat Stripe retainer as outside income for Maya (personal tax). I'll do the country risk report and post here by EOD tomorrow.
Priya (Legal): agree with Marco. If she’ll be contracting for a US client while physically in ID, advise she avoid signing any local contracts as a Redwood rep. Also recommend she does not invoice under Redwood.
Ava (People Ops): thanks. To keep this lightweight: Maya, please submit the "short-term remote" form with travel dates and home-base confirmation. Manager to approve there. Payroll/Legal — can you post any concrete flags by 48 hours? I'll hold stipend payment changes until we have confirmation.
PeopleOpsBot: Reminder — submit short-term remote form: https://redwood-internal/self-serve/remote-form (form fields: dates, location, contact, intended work).
Maya Patel: done — I submitted the form and attached client retainer details (no Redwood involvement).
Marco (Payroll): got the form, running the Indonesia check now. Quick note: if local authorities assert source-of-income rules, we might be asked to register a withholding agent after even short engagements; probability low but not zero.
Priya (Legal): I'll loop in our APAC counsel for a brief read (1-2 business days). If counsel flags risk > low, we'll propose options (stagger travel, reduce client work while abroad, or temporary payroll withholding).
Ava (People Ops): summary of next steps: 1) Payroll — country risk report (EOD tomorrow), 2) Legal — counsel read (48h), 3) Manager — confirm stipend approval in form, 4) Maya — hold off invoicing as "Redwood" or using company resources while abroad. We'll reconvene here once both reports are in. Thanks all. :pray:
Devon (Manager): approved stipend on the form.
Maya Patel: thanks all — I appreciate the check. I'll pause any client invoicing until final.
PeopleOpsBot: Thread archived after inactivity.
